problem.text: Issue #2 reports a wheel-build rejection of absolute source paths under Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.6; the quoted error requires paths relative to setup.py.

reasoning.text: The merge replaces abspath with relpath anchored at dirname(__file__), retaining the complete discovered source path rather than dropping nested directories.

impact.text: This addresses the reported path-format rejection without changing source selection or compiler settings. A PR commenter reports that the change fixed their error.

source_notes.text: The earlier packaging entry describes the same setup-relative path fix; this merge incorporates that change.
The PR explicitly claims to fix issue #2, and the maintainer acknowledges an oversight.

limitations: No wheel build or native compilation was executed. The standard-library path check assumes the working directory is the setup directory; it does not validate Windows separators or invocation from another directory.

claims.text: setup.py recursively collects .c, .cpp and .cu files from exllamav3/exllamav3_ext. When precompilation is enabled and PyTorch is available, sources feeds CUDAExtension, and setup_kwargs passes that extension and BuildExtension to setuptools.

The replacement changes only path representation. Keeping os.path.join(root, file) preserves nested source locations, while anchoring relpath to setup.py supplies the relative representation requested by the reported error.

A standard-library transcription over the first-parent checkout found 16 eligible sources, eight nested. With the checkout root as the setup directory, every replacement path was relative and resolved to the same target as the original absolute path.

annotation.summary: Merges the setup.py fix that supplies setup-relative native source paths instead of absolute paths, addressing the reported wheel-build rejection.

argv:
import os
base=os.getcwd()
paths=[os.path.join(r,f) for r,_,fs in os.walk('exllamav3/exllamav3_ext') for f in fs if f.endswith(('.c','.cpp','.cu'))]
new=[os.path.relpath(p,start=base) for p in paths]
assert paths
assert all(not os.path.isabs(p) for p in new)
assert all(os.path.abspath(a)==os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base,b)) for a,b in zip(paths,new))
print({'sources':len(paths),'nested':sum(os.path.dirname(p)!='exllamav3/exllamav3_ext' for p in paths),'all_relative':True,'same_targets':True})
